dedupeRule: Before preparing or sending anything, search OpenClaw targets, drafts, send_log, suppression, and the recipient domain. Never create a second active draft for the same prospect and angle.
measurementRule: Record earned editorial links, unlinked mentions, directory listings, podcast appearances, partnerships, sponsorships, replies and referral leads as separate outcomes.

prospects.fitEvidence: The public guest page invites financiers and topics involving debt, private capital and lender nuance, and says guest participation has no cost.
prospects.contribution: Why urgent property finance fails before the lender sees it: title position, peak debt and exit-evidence checks for developers.
prospects.draftSubject: Guest idea: decision-ready urgent property finance
prospects.draftBody: Your guest page specifically welcomes financiers and discussions of debt and private capital. An Emet Capital principal could contribute a practical, non-promotional episode on why urgent property-finance requests stall before lender assessment: unclear title position, understated peak debt and an exit that is plausible but not evidenced. The discussion could give developers a reusable readiness checklist and clearly distinguish a fast initial assessment from a guaranteed settlement. If this fits your editorial calendar, we can send a short outline and speaker background for review.

prospects.fitEvidence: The public contact page invites property professionals and explicitly lists finance and mortgage brokers as potential guests.
prospects.contribution: Open versus closed bridging exits and why a lower periodic repayment is not necessarily a lower total bridge cost.
prospects.draftSubject: Podcast idea: comparing the real cost of a property bridge
prospects.draftBody: Your contact page invites finance and mortgage professionals to contribute to the property conversation. An Emet Capital principal could offer a practical segment on open versus closed bridging exits, peak-debt modelling and why a lower repayment can still produce a higher total cost once retained interest, fees and timing are included. The aim would be an educational framework listeners can use, not a product pitch. If useful, we can provide a concise episode outline and supporting decision checklist.

prospects.fitEvidence: The contributor guidelines accept eligible Australian small-business owners and reject PR or SEO-agency submissions; an eligible Emet principal must author and submit any contribution in their own voice.
prospects.contribution: The equipment repayment trap: matching useful life, residual, downtime and total contractual payments before an SME signs.
prospects.draftSubject: Contributor idea: four equipment-finance numbers SMEs miss
prospects.draftBody: Proposed article: four equipment-finance numbers an SME should model before signing—economic useful life, downtime exposure, residual or balloon amount, and total contractual payments including known fees. It would explain why a monthly-payment comparison can be misleading, separate finance analysis from tax advice, and use a worked decision framework without quoting promotional market rates. This must be reviewed, rewritten where needed and submitted directly by an eligible Emet Capital principal under Flying Solo's contributor rules.

prospects.fitEvidence: The podcast page includes a guest application and covers property, business and entrepreneurship for an Australian audience.
prospects.contribution: When short-term property finance solves a timing gap and when it merely delays a structural cash-flow problem.
prospects.draftSubject: Guest idea: timing gap or structural funding problem?
prospects.draftBody: A practical conversation on diagnosing whether short-term property finance resolves a defined timing mismatch or simply moves an unresolved cash-flow problem into a more expensive period. The framework would cover purpose, peak debt, downside cases and evidenced exits, with clear boundaries around individual advice and lender outcomes. Hold until the first-wave podcast drafts have been reviewed to avoid overlapping outreach.

prospects.fitEvidence: The site provides a public editorial contact and broker-listing route, but its predominantly residential audience requires a tightly bounded commercial-purpose angle.
prospects.contribution: How business-purpose property finance differs from consumer home lending and why the purpose boundary matters.
prospects.draftSubject: Expert source: the business-purpose boundary in property finance
prospects.draftBody: Offer an attributable, carefully bounded explanation of how business-purpose property finance differs from a consumer home loan, including why borrower purpose, security and legal context should be established before comparing products. Do not pitch a generic link insertion. Hold unless an editor is working on a directly relevant story or resource.
